title: Cross-host Linux and macOS effect evidence
description: Objective: collect production-surface effect conformance evidence on actual Linux and macOS hosts for every frozen platform boundary, bound to one exact source commit and distribution. Deliverable: host-native fault schedules/evidence receipts and a reproducible cross-host aggregation protocol. NOT in scope: implementing platform classifiers, running off-host fixtures as proof, or weakening Windows behavior. Hard dependencies: Linux boundary task-f01ef545b1554a2cb5df340ce78f6a5c, macOS boundary task-45d12ecfa6ae4938b23af28fe7876a44, doctor task-1cafc7f9fcdc4c9299860b6b1e38275d, and distribution packaging task-739879d0d1ce4a7ea4d1430688cdc4dc. Measured at HEAD 30458af on win32: tests/fault/linux/** and tests/fault/macos/** are absent; archived tasks-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275/e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 have no landing commits, and their reopen notes explicitly require live Linux/macOS hosts. Consumer: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93. Owned paths: tests/fault/linux/**, tests/fault/macos/**, cross-host evidence manifests/aggregation, and CI/host runner configuration only where approved.
definitionOfDone: On an actual Linux host and an actual macOS host, every hand-written PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES member runs crash-before/after activation and cancellation schedules against the production classifier/runner surface; each schedule asserts exact PROVEN/UNKNOWN code, layer, boundary, and a nonzero case count.

Each host record binds source commit, distribution manifest/digest, OS/kernel/arch, Node/pnpm/provider runtime closure, fixture/fault schedule digests, timestamps, and raw run receipts; unverifiable or mismatched bindings yield UNKNOWN and never PASS.
Linux and macOS receipts are canonical, immutable, independently verifiable, and aggregated without trusting caller-selected host claims; missing host evidence leaves only that OS row UNKNOWN.
No off-host test fixture, emulation label, or design claim is accepted as host proof; Windows stays a separate observation and is not weakened.
Host-native fault gates and the cross-host verifier exit 0, and task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 is recorded as the acceptance consumer.
taskRails: This task requires real Linux and macOS execution environments; do not claim completion from win32 alone.
Use production @moe/runner/platform and distribution/doctor surfaces, not test reimplementations.
Every refusal/unknown asserts stable code plus layer/boundary and every generated schedule asserts positive cardinality.

implementationPlan.description: Start RED with hostile contract/aggregation tests and two hand-written host suites. In the cross-host fault test, specify exact-key immutable receipt/aggregate versions, canonical bytes and self-digest rules, fixed expected host slots (`linux`, `darwin`), and frozen failure layers `CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR` / `CROSS_HOST_AGGREGATOR` with exact codes `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_MALFORMED`, `CROSS_HOST_HOST_UNVERIFIABLE`, `CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_SOURCE_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIABLE`, `CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULE_INCOMPLETE`, `CROSS_HOST_SCHEDULE_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RAW_RECEIPT_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_MISSING`, and `CROSS_HOST_RECEIPT_DUPLICATE`. Generate tamper cases for every binding, assert the generated count is positive, and assert exact code, layer, host slot, and `UNKNOWN` rather than only failure. In each OS suite, independently hand-name the production seven-boundary tuple and three schedules (`CRASH_BEFORE_ACTIVATION`, `CRASH_AFTER_ACTIVATION`, `CANCELLATION`), assert the 7x3 product is exactly 21 unique cases, and make the matching-host path fail until the real driver exists; a wrong host must assert `CROSS_HOST_HOST_MISMATCH` at `CROSS_HOST_COLLECTOR`, emit no PROVEN receipt, and never be skipped as proof.

Implement the typed evidence protocol, not a replacement platform classifier. Provide sorted-key UTF-8 canonical encoding, SHA-256 projection/digest helpers, total exact-key decoders, deep-frozen accepted values, content-addressed receipt/aggregate filenames, `verifyHostReceipt(expectedSlot, bytes, expectedSourceAndDistribution)`, and an aggregator over the fixed Linux/darwin slots. A receipt must bind Git source SHA/object format; all six canonical distribution components with manifest and asset digests plus a common aggregate digest; production doctor OS/arch/Node/pnpm report and its digest; kernel; production provider runtime observation/closure and digest; schedule/fixture/config/workflow/lockfile digests; canonical timestamps; exactly 21 raw case records and their digests; receipt version/digest; and consumer `task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93`. Verification must recompute every digest and derive the row from verified doctor/runtime identity rather than a caller host claim or artifact name. A missing, malformed, duplicate, stale-source, distribution-divergent, runtime-unverifiable, incomplete, or tampered input yields a frozen UNKNOWN row with the exact code/layer; one bad or absent slot must not erase the other slot's valid row.

Implement the shared real-host schedule driver using only Node built-ins and public package roots. Derive the executing host from `collectDoctorVersionReport()` plus `os.release()`, never a matrix/env claim. For each unique case, create unique effect/grant/process identities (the verifier registry is process-global), use production activation, and invoke the OS child launcher only after ACTIVATED. Before-activation schedules tombstone first, assert zero physical launch plus `EFFECT_TOMBSTONED` / `ACTIVATION` / `detail.leg=tombstoneWitness`, then classify an absent fact as `UNKNOWN` with `PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT`, the exact OS layer, and exact boundary. After-activation crash schedules wait for a real `process.execPath` verifier child to start, SIGKILL and observe it, assert `VERIFIER_PROCESS_EXIT_AMBIGUOUS` / `CAPTURE` / source `PROCESS`, and feed production `classifyCrash`; cancellation schedules start the real child, request ACTIVE cancellation (`MUST_DRAIN`), abort/observe it, assert `VERIFIER_PROCESS_CANCELLED` / `CAPTURE` / source `PROCESS`, and feed production `reconcileClaudeRun`. Build each boundary fact through its owner: runtime observation from the actual Node executable bytes/closure, scope plus input manifest with at least one tracked path, a real temp symlink/lstat/realpath observation, activation commit lease binding, reconciliation, and crash classification. Invoke the appropriate production boundary classifier for every case and the production whole-platform observer for every seven-case schedule batch; record exact truth/code/layer/boundary and raw process/timing/digest facts. Use bounded waits and `finally` cleanup so no child or temp path survives.

Finish the thin Linux/macOS suites and add the Node 24 collector/aggregator CLI. The Linux file must pin `linux`/`PLATFORM_LINUX`; the macOS file must pin `darwin`/`PLATFORM_MACOS`; on-host they run all 21 cases, assert the exact runner and platform outcomes, positive launch/case counts, and write only raw schedule evidence to a bounded requested directory. The `.mjs` CLI must call the real `buildReleaseSubject` (kept out of the TS import graph because `tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json` otherwise raises TS7016), generate an ephemeral Ed25519 verification key, and retain only source-bound unsigned manifest/asset digests for cross-host identity—never compare key-dependent container/signature digests. Its `collect` mode combines an on-host raw schedule with fresh Git/release/doctor/runtime/file measurements and writes a content-addressed canonical receipt; its `aggregate` mode rebuilds the expected source/distribution from the checked-out commit, reads the two fixed slot directories, verifies both independently, always writes a canonical aggregate, and exits nonzero under `--require-complete` unless both rows are PROVEN. Invalid CLI/input paths must return a structured exact CROSS_HOST code/layer, not throw. Exercise both CLI modes from the fault test with temp directories; fixture-generated outputs are integrity tests only and are never labeled host proof.

Extend (do not weaken or replace) the existing cross-host workflow with an independent `host-evidence` include-matrix whose exact job names are `host-evidence-linux` on `ubuntu-latest` and `host-evidence-darwin` on `macos-latest`, plus `cross-host-aggregate`. Keep pinned Node 24.16.0/pnpm 11.0.8, frozen install, `permissions: contents: read`, fail-fast false, and the existing broad gate unchanged so foreign baseline red remains visible. Each host job compiles the fault tree, runs only its matching fault file under the serial fault Vitest config, captures the real Vitest status through `PIPESTATUS[0]`, requires nonzero `Test Files` and `Tests` lines and the internal `executedCaseCount=21`, runs collector mode, and uploads `cross-host-{linux|darwin}-${{ github.sha }}` with upload-artifact v4 and `if-no-files-found:error`. The aggregate job depends only on the evidence matrix and uses `if: always()`: checkout the same SHA, download each artifact into its fixed expectation slot (transport names confer no authority), run the focused hostile contract test with nonzero counts, run aggregate mode `--require-complete`, and upload `cross-host-aggregate-${{ github.sha }}` even on refusal. No Windows source/test/workflow behavior is changed, and no off-host fixture or matrix variable can produce PROVEN.

Perform the single adversarial review after implementation and before the final gate. Read the complete owned-path diff as an attacker; verify no test/helper reimplements platform, activation, cancellation, crash, doctor, or distribution authority; no caller-selected host, artifact name, elapsed quiet, classifier envelope, or missing fact can upgrade UNKNOWN; all children/temp paths are cleaned; and the existing broad/Windows behavior is intact. Re-run the hostile mutation sweep for extra/missing keys, host spoof, wrong source, one manifest and asset digest, doctor/runtime closure, schedule universe, one raw case, self-digest/filename, duplicate receipt, and each missing host, asserting positive mutation cardinality and the exact code/layer/slot. Temporarily mutate the owned verifier/driver production surface so a refusal maps to the wrong code or bypasses the imported production classifier, confirm the relevant test goes red, restore it, then confirm green. Check every non-test helper (`effect-evidence-contract.ts`, `effect-schedule-driver.ts`, and the `.mjs` CLI) is <=250 physical lines, no scratch/generated evidence is tracked, and `git diff --check` is clean. Stage only the seven explicit owned paths, remove any foreign staged entry, commit by explicit pathspec, verify `git show --stat`, and request authorized human/governor publication of the exact committed SHA; never push it yourself.

Run the one concentrated final gate on the exact committed/published SHA. First re-run every repo-wide command captured in step 1 and report the merge-base-vs-HEAD failing-path delta verbatim; completion requires no new failure intersecting the seven owned paths, while foreign baseline red is disclosed rather than called green. Then run this exact completion command and retain its fresh output (including nonzero local Vitest counts): `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json && pnpm exec vitest run --config tests/fault/vitest.config.ts cross-host/effect-evidence.fault.ts cross-host/production-surfaces.fault.ts && node --input-type=module -e 'import{execFileSync}from"node:child_process";const sha=execFileSync("git",["rev-parse","HEAD"],{encoding:"utf8"}).trim(),base="https://api.github.com/repos/yaront1111/Moe-NG",headers={Accept:"application/vnd.github+json","X-GitHub-Api-Version":"2022-11-28"},get=async p=>{const r=await fetch(base+p,{headers});if(!r.ok)throw Error(`${r.status} ${p}`);return r.json()},requiredJobs=["host-evidence-linux","host-evidence-darwin","cross-host-aggregate"];const runs=(await get(`/actions/workflows/cross-host.yml/runs?head_sha=${sha}&per_page=20`)).workflow_runs.filter(r=>r.head_sha===sha&&r.status==="completed");let proof=null;for(const run of runs){const jobs=(await get(`/actions/runs/${run.id}/jobs?per_page=100`)).jobs;if(requiredJobs.every(n=>jobs.some(j=>j.name===n&&j.status==="completed"&&j.conclusion==="success"))){proof={run,jobs};break}}if(!proof)throw Error(`no exact-SHA Linux/macOS/aggregate success for ${sha}`);const artifacts=(await get(`/actions/runs/${proof.run.id}/artifacts?per_page=100`)).artifacts,requiredArtifacts=[`cross-host-linux-${sha}`,`cross-host-darwin-${sha}`,`cross-host-aggregate-${sha}`];for(const n of requiredArtifacts){const a=artifacts.find(x=>x.name===n);if(!a||a.expired||a.size_in_bytes<=0||typeof a.digest!=="string"||!a.digest.startsWith("sha256:"))throw Error(`missing/unverifiable artifact ${n}`)}console.log(JSON.stringify({sha,run:proof.run.html_url,jobs:requiredJobs,artifacts:requiredArtifacts}))'`. Inspect the three successful job logs and record their positive Vitest counts, both `executedCaseCount=21` lines, exact Linux/darwin receipt digests, and aggregate PROVEN rows. If the authorized exact-SHA publication/run is unavailable, or either host/aggregate job is not green, report blocked instead of substituting WSL, fixtures, an older SHA, or the overall workflow conclusion; after any fix, repeat steps 7-8 against the new committed SHA.
